title: Propensity Inference: Environmental Contributors to LLM Behaviour
authors: Olli Jarviniemi, Robert Kirk, Ben Millwood et al. (UK AISI)
summary: Develops methods to measure LLM propensity for undesired behavior by decomposing the influence of 12 environmental variables (strategic vs non-strategic) across 23 models and 11 environments, to inform AI control risk assessment.
key_result: Strategic and non-strategic factors contribute roughly equally to behavior, with no evidence strategic factors grow more influential as capabilities increase.
open_threads: Turning theoretical frameworks/cognitive models of AI decision-making into empirically testable forms; deeper mechanistic understanding.

title: Security Stress Test: Exposing the Brittleness of DeepSeek-V4-Pro's Safeguards
authors: Lukas Struppek, Heather McIntyre, Kellin Pelrine (FAR AI)
summary: Adversarial red-team of the open-weight DeepSeek-V4-Pro across CBRN, cyberattack, and terrorism-related prompts; the model blocks 100% of direct harmful requests but collapses under three adversarial attack strategies.
key_result: Attack success rates of 98-100% across every harm domain; jailbroken model retains near-full baseline utility, producing detailed harmful responses.
open_threads: Safeguards are superficial; building safeguards robust to jailbreaks rather than surface-level refusals; coverage limited to one model and three attack families.

title: CAISI Evaluation of DeepSeek V4 Pro
authors: Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), NIST
summary: CAISI independently evaluates open-weight DeepSeek V4 Pro across cyber, software engineering, natural sciences, abstract reasoning, and mathematics, comparing against leading US models using 16 benchmarks over 35 models.
key_result: DeepSeek V4 Pro lags the frontier by ~8 months (IRT Elo 800+-28); most capable PRC model CAISI has evaluated but trails frontier US offerings, with better cost efficiency.
open_threads: SWE-Bench scores differ due to scaffolding choices; some results statistically imputed; DeepSeek self-reported benchmarks overstate performance.

title: Evaluating Offline Monitoring of Internal AI Agents
summary: Argues current public reporting on the effectiveness of offline monitoring of internally deployed AI agents is insufficient: companies disclose only initial flagging rates without accounting for downstream pipeline filtering or human-review escalation.
key_result: Public reporting on offline monitoring effectiveness is insufficient to assess true detection capability because firms omit downstream filtering and escalation data.
open_threads: Only Anthropic/OpenAI disclosed monitoring info; whether synthetic red-team attacks reflect real misalignment; the flagging-to-escalation gap.

title: Comprehensive AI Governance Requires Addressing Non-Model Capability Gains
authors: Arthur Goemans, Noemi Dreksler, Allan Dafoe et al. (GovAI)
summary: Challenges the model-centric paradigm of AI governance, showing capability gains increasingly come from outside the base model (inference gains, systems gains, asset gains), and argues pre-deployment model evaluation alone is becoming inadequate.
key_result: Model-level governance becomes less effective as progress is increasingly driven by non-model gains; governance must expand to system, entity, agent, cloud levels plus societal resilience.
open_threads: Future impacts of embodiment, continual learning, AI diffusion; concrete mechanisms for higher-level governance not fully specified.
